principles: Preserve disciplined spacing and mutual support while creating local sword superiority at the decisive point.
Use movement, observation, concise signals, terrain, and controlled pressure to deny clean enemy choices before committing to the finish.
Maintain a usable reserve or reaction option whenever the objective permits; do not exhaust every capable fighter in the opening exchange.
Capture, restraint, disengagement, or lethal force follow mission authority and tactical necessity rather than pride or uncontrolled pursuit.
Break contact and reform when command, cohesion, casualty extraction, or objective geometry is lost; elite status is not permission for wasteful attrition.
Command succession, casualty handling, equipment discipline, and information preservation are part of combat effectiveness rather than rear-area concerns.
